title: Function

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Follow one input through a rule to its unique output, and distinguish the rule from its current value.
meaning: A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain. The playground illustrates the affine family f(x)=ax+b: x moves through a fixed rule; a and b edit the rule itself.

definition.setting: A function between declared sets; the executable specimen is a bounded real affine family.
definition.formal_latex: f:A\to B,\quad\forall x\in A\;\exists!\,y\in B:\;y=f(x).\qquad f_{a,b}(x)=ax+b.

signature.general: f:A→B; exactly one output for each x∈A
signature.x: input in A; real x∈[−5,5] in this specimen
signature.output: a×x+b; its units are the output units

conditions: Every allowed input has exactly one assigned output.
A function includes its declared domain; a formula alone need not settle the intended domain.
For the illustrated family, x, a and b are finite and within the declared control bounds.
A multiplier and offset require compatible units; changing a or b changes the selected function.
definition.domain_notes: General functions need not be numerical, affine, continuous or invertible. In this specimen the input domain is [−5,5], and each chosen a,b has range [b−5|a|,b+5|a|]. Bounds are a display/model contract, not a restriction on the mathematical concept.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; affine properties are author-derived. No independent review or general theorem-proving claimed.

grammar.pronunciation: f of x equals a times x plus b
grammar.formation_rule: scaled=a*x; output=scaled+b; input=x. For each selected a,b this is a fixed affine function on x∈[−5,5].
grammar.precedence: Evaluate ax before adding b; f(x) denotes function application, not f multiplied by x.

prompts.prompt: Does f(2)=5 tell you the entire function?
prompts.answer: No. It gives one input–output pair; many distinct rules agree there.

prompts.prompt: Why can a horizontal line be a function?
prompts.answer: Each input has one output even when all inputs share that output.
